prerequisites: Knowledge from the Business Administration submodule.

learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to create transparency and understanding for the often 'nebulous' topic and to show clear structures and practical work aids.

Participants should be able to know, understand, and explain in simple words after the course: what the relevant components of the presented processes/systems/organization are, to what extent it affects them (role, tasks, responsibility, benefit), and how the relevant process flows are enriched in this regard.
Participants should also be able to make the relevant requirements for their own work area transparent as goals and to fulfill them.
By presenting the value contributions of the system/processes for companies/organization and employees, awareness, interest, and motivation for 'proactive living' of the system should be generated.

Participants in the areas of Compliance, Data Protection, and IT Law should acquire basic knowledge and be enabled to develop practical solutions for relevant problems in this area, even in the form of procedural instructions and process descriptions for standard problems.
Furthermore, it is expected that after completing this module, participants can explain the relevant content understandably in their own words.

Participants are able to conceptualize and implement a digitized Integrated Management System in the areas of Compliance, Data Protection, and IT Law, or relevant process flows, and to enrich the organizational structure and processes with appropriate Compliance, Risk, and IKS components.
Participants can solve problem cases using the judicial case resolution method.
Participants can implement the acquired knowledge in companies/organizations through target-actual comparisons and recommendations for action.
Participants have the ability to assign facts and tasks to the appropriate area in the company or environment and to recognize interfaces to other functions.
Using SWOT analyses, target-actual comparisons, etc., participants are able to make recommendations for action to manage governance (corporate management and monitoring) risks.

Participants know the methods of audits and primarily orient themselves on the 'Current State of Legislation and Jurisprudence (Compliance)' and secondarily on the 'Recognized State of Science and Practice' regarding relevant topics. In doing so, they consult the generally known standards (rules (international) institutionalized expert bodies) (e.g., DIN/ISO/COSO/IDW/DIIR/etc.).

Participants are able to understand the networking within the various corporate functions (management, core, and support process topics) and to conceptualize and improve a corresponding architecture, taking into account the legal framework.

SWOT analyses and target-actual comparisons within the framework of practical activity in the company (or based on case studies) enable participants to improve the organization of companies or sub-areas in their professional lives.

Participants reflect on the topic in an international context (e.g., international law, international standards), participants reflect all content under the aspect of Digital Transformation and modeling as process flows.
